clue.text: Do away with tax

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cut out or remove
second meaning: a duty levied on goods made at home

explanation.surface: A campaigner calls for a tax to be scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: One word is both a verb for cutting something out and a noun for a duty on home-produced goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To excise is to remove surgically or strike out, and excise duty is a government levy on goods.

clue.text: Obscure excerpts from film in Early English

indicators.note: in places the excerpts inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: EE is the standard abbreviation for Early English
film excerpts are clips

explanation.surface: Little-known extracts from a film made in Early English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' reads as an adjective; here it is the verb meaning to block out.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse is to hide or block the light of something, just as to obscure is.

clue.text: Topless club started by college kid

definitions.note: the Cisco Kid, a fictional Western hero

indicators.note: topless means without a top, so the first letter is dropped
started by says the next piece goes at the front

parts.note: C is a standard abbreviation for college
a dance club

explanation.surface: A student runs a topless nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' is not a child: it is the second word of the Cisco Kid, the Western character, so the answer is his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cisco Kid was a famous Western cowboy hero of films, radio and television, named after this word.

clue.text: Goes around introducing first lover to second partners

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: introducing means bringing it in among the others, inside them

parts.note: wives are marriage partners

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the initial letter of this word

explanation.surface: A philanderer brings a new lover to meet his second wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The lover's initial slips in before the last letter of WIVES, all after S.
explanation.definitionFit: To swivel is to turn around on a pivot, so swivels means turns or goes around.

clue.text: Kind of oil, which helps things to run smoothly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the oil pressed from a bean, famous as a laxative

definitions.text: which helps things to run smoothly
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a small swivelling wheel fixed under furniture

explanation.surface: An oil praised as a lubricant that keeps machinery running smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pretends both halves describe one lubricating oil; the second half is really the little wheel under a chair or trolley.
explanation.definitionFit: Castor oil is a known variety, and a castor is a small wheel letting furniture roll easily across floors.

clue.text: Acknowledgement of a letter delivered

indicators.note: delivered as a speech is spoken out, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a letter such as A or E is a vowel

explanation.surface: Confirmation that a letter has arrived in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter delivered' suggests the post; the letter is one of the alphabet and 'delivered' means spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: An avowal is an open declaration or admission, which is an acknowledgement of something.

clue.text: Reactionary transport board will be easy to lead

indicators.note: a reactionary wants to go backwards, so the vehicle is written in reverse

parts.note: a cart is a means of transport
a board can be a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A conservative transport board will be easily steered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reactionary' looks like politics, describing the board; it tells you to reverse the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractable person or animal is docile and manageable, readily controlled or guided.

clue.text: Welder without money raised a screen

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards, from the bottom
without money says the abbreviation for pounds sterling is taken out

parts.note: a solderer joins metal, a kind of welder

explanation.surface: A penniless welder put up a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for pounds, from the Latin libra. SOLDERER without it is SODERER, which reads upwards as REREDOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen or partition behind a church altar.

clue.text: Dreaming Rovers failing MOT, lass is numb

indicators.note: a failing car is broken down, so the letters are put together another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl is numb after her Rover cars fail the MOT test.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover was a British car make, and the MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepwalkers wander about while asleep, so they are rovers who are dreaming.

clue.text: More unmarked fruit

indicators.note: un- marks an absence, so the abbreviation for the old German mark is struck out

parts.note: a stone fruit, in the plural

explanation.surface: Extra fruit that has no blemishes on it.
explanation.walkthrough: M stands for the mark, the old German currency; taking it out of PLUMS leaves PLUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Plus is used as an adjective or noun meaning additional, extra or something added beyond.

clue.text: New location on-line for image-worship

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the line comes at the end
something new has been remade, so these letters are set in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
RY is the usual abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A new website location where people can go to worship images online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On-line' looks like internet jargon, but it splits: 'on' places the railway line after the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: Iconolatry is the veneration of icons or religious pictures, literally the worship of images.

clue.text: First of old parliamentarians with attitude, getting cross

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of each following word

parts.note: the initial letters of these two words
a pose is an attitude struck or adopted

explanation.surface: Old MPs with attitude growing angry in the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry; here it is the verb meaning to go against someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross a person is to thwart or go against them, which is what opposing means.

clue.text: Twice each month one has small ups and downs

definitions.text: Twice each month one has small ups and downs

parts.words: Twice each month one has small ups and downs
parts.note: surface reading: someone with a regular, mild mood swing
setter's reading: the sea's smallest rise and fall, which comes around the first and third quarters of the moon

explanation.surface: Someone whose moods go up and down a little twice a month.
explanation.definitionFit: Neap tides occur twice in each lunar month and have the least difference between high and low water.

clue.text: Dreary River Oise breaking over motorway

indicators.note: in an across clue, over means coming just before, so the road follows

parts.note: the Wear is a river in north-east England, through Durham

indicators.note: a word that breaks falls apart, and its letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: A dull river, the Oise, bursting its banks over a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River' is not the Oise: it is a second river, the Wear, while the French name is just letters to rearrange with the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearisome describes something tiresome and tedious, which is what dreary means of a task or day.

clue.text: Blue uniform shirt issued once in a blue moon

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for the noun answer: a thing that occurs only very seldom

parts.note: blue steak is cooked so lightly it is very underdone
uniform means regular, level
a T-shirt, the letter named after its shape

explanation.surface: A blue uniform shirt is handed out only very rarely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' twice in the clue misleads: the first is a steak order, the second belongs to the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Once in a blue moon means very seldom, so something occurring that way is uncommon.

clue.text: One twice got the bird

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
bis is Latin for twice, called out for an encore

explanation.surface: A performer gave an encore and was booed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got the bird' is theatre slang for being hissed; here 'the bird' is simply the definition. Bis appears in musical scores to mean repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading fowl with a curved bill, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: See 25
Monster returns, supporting Mao's introduction to China

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting below, so this goes underneath
an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: the initial letter of the name

indicators.note: returns means comes back, so the monster's name is written backwards

parts.note: the Loch Ness monster's nickname

explanation.surface: A monster comes back to back Mao as he is introduced to China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is lower-case china, porcelain; the capital C is only at the start of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Meissen is a fine German porcelain, so it is a type of china for the table.

clue.text: Freedom fighters in holy city shortly to take up pilgrimage, you say?

indicators.note: the shortened city takes in the other pieces, holding them inside
shortly means cut short, so the final letter of the city is dropped

parts.note: Medina is Islam's second holy city

indicators.note: say asks for a letter that is pronounced like the pronoun before it

parts.note: the letter U sounds like the pronoun

indicators.note: turned up means turned back on itself, so the pilgrimage is written backwards

parts.note: the hajj, the pilgrimage to Mecca, is also spelt haj

explanation.surface: Guerrillas based in a holy city setting out on a pilgrimage.
explanation.walkthrough: MEDIN is Medina shortened; U and the turned-round JAH go inside it after the M, giving MUJAHEDIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Mujahedin are Islamic guerrilla fighters, notably those resisting Soviet occupation in Afghanistan, often styled freedom fighters.

clue.text: Balmy Mr Capp carrying nowt to Tyneside

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so the nothing goes inside

parts.note: Andy Capp, the cartoon working man from north-east England
nowt is northern dialect for nothing, a zero
Tyneside is in the North East of England

explanation.surface: Cartoon character Andy Capp, a bit barmy, bringing nothing to Tyneside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balmy' sounds like barmy, mad; here it means soothing. Andy Capp is a long-running Daily Mirror strip cartoon character.
explanation.definitionFit: An anodyne is a painkiller, so as an adjective it means soothing or mild, like a balm.

clue.text: One can produce a score when rising composer (no saint) catches cold

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means read from the bottom up
catches means holds within, so the cold goes inside
no saint tells you to drop the abbreviation for saint

parts.note: the Italian opera composer
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A rising composer needs a cold to produce a score.
explanation.walkthrough: A score here is a scratch or cut, not music. ROSSINI loses one S for saint, then reads upward as INISOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An incisor is a sharp front cutting tooth, so it can score or notch something it bites.

clue.text: Meat for each basket

parts.note: ham is a cured meat
per means for each, as in per head

explanation.surface: Meat for each person, packed in a picnic basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamper is a large lidded wicker basket, often used for picnics or food gifts.

clue.text: Well-read people in orbit are tilting over

indicators.note: tilting over suggests tipping all the way, so the letters run backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters straddling these three words

explanation.surface: Educated people in space, tipping over as they orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, orbIT ARE TILting gives LITERATI.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are the educated, literary class, people widely read in books and letters.

clue.text: Service post

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a form of church worship
second meaning: a position or job of authority

explanation.walkthrough: 'Service post' reads like the mail, but the words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a prescribed liturgical rite in church, and also a position of responsibility someone holds.

clue.text: Flippant cashier promises to pay for small plane

indicators.note: to cashier is to dismiss from service, so these letters are thrown out

parts.note: facetious means flippant, not serious
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A flippant bank cashier promises to repay the cost of a light aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cashier' looks like a bank clerk; it is the verb to dismiss. 'Plane' is a flat surface, not an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A facet is one of the small flat cut surfaces on a gemstone, a little plane.

clue.text: So upset, doctor runs off to therapy to get treatment ?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are mixed up
to doctor is to tamper with, which also calls for rearranging
something that runs off has left, so the cricket abbreviation for runs is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written; R for runs comes out of it

explanation.surface: An upset patient's doctor runs off to therapy for treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person in the story, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange. R is the cricket abbreviation for runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteopathy is a form of manual therapy that manipulates bones and muscles, a kind of medical care.

clue.text: Stuff dough and what goes with Cumbrian butter
The birds and the bees and a flower finished off King Cole

indicators.note: finished off says this piece completes the word, coming at its end

parts.note: Nat King Cole was an American singer
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure runs through Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Birds, bees and a flower polished off old King Cole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finished off' places the river at the end of the singer's first name. A flower in crosswords is often a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds and bees, plants and animals, are the natural world, so they stand for the whole of nature.

clue.text: A pointer for a Bunthorne?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gun dog, a breed related to the pointer, that indicates game
second meaning: Bunthorne was a well-known Guardian crossword compiler

explanation.walkthrough: Bunthorne was a pseudonym used by a Guardian crossword compiler, so he is an example of a puzzle maker; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a gun dog that indicates game, and also the person who composes a crossword.
